current_definition: An unpleasant or far-reaching result that follows an event, felt some time after the original cause.
To cause a large number of new things—often problems, ideas, or other events—to come into being at once.
A catastrophic event that causes enormous destruction or brings about the end of a way of life; complete and final ruin.
The process by which something gradually breaks apart, comes to an end, or loses its form.
Lasting for only a very short time by its very nature; fleeting in a way that cannot be changed.
A pause or gap in an activity or process, during which nothing happens for a period of time.
Just beginning to develop or appear; in the earliest, barely noticeable stage of a process.
Able to be shaped, changed, or influenced without breaking; adaptable to new conditions.
A complete and usually dramatic change in form, character, or nature—often one that happens over time.
Of central importance to how something develops; describing the one moment or factor on which everything else depends.
Happening very suddenly and steeply, especially a sharp decline or drop.
Happening only occasionally and at irregular intervals, with no clear pattern.
Passing through or lasting only a short time; present briefly before moving on.
Unfavorable or harmful; working against success or well-being in a way that makes progress difficult.
Requiring a very great amount of effort, endurance, or hard work over a long period of time.
A gradual reduction in numbers, strength, or resources through sustained pressure, loss, or wear rather than a single blow.
To make someone or something very weak and unable to function properly, especially through prolonged strain or damage.
Causing harm or damage, especially in a way that builds up gradually and may not be noticed at first.
To gradually move into or take over an area, right, or domain that belongs to someone else, often in small steps.
An urgent situation or pressing demand that requires immediate attention or action; a condition of great difficulty or need.
To free someone or something from a difficult, complicated, or dangerous situation that it is trapped in.
Something that restricts freedom of action or progress; a constraint that limits what someone can do.
A complicated and confusing network of rules, processes, or paths that is very difficult to navigate or find a way through.
Involving a very heavy burden of work, responsibility, or difficulty; more demanding than seems fair or reasonable.
Very strict and demanding, leaving very little room for exceptions or flexibility; applied with great severity.
A free and uncontrolled outpouring of words, feelings, or liquid.
So delicate and light as to seem not of this physical world; airy and almost heavenly in quality.
Lasting only a very short time before vanishing; tending to fade and disappear quickly.
Glowing intensely with light or heat; brilliantly bright.
Giving off or full of light; brightly glowing.
Showing deep understanding or insight; intellectually penetrating far below the surface.
To give off small flashes of light; to sparkle.
Having real importance, meaning, or value; solid and significant rather than superficial.
Able to be defended, supported, or maintained against challenge or criticism; reasonable enough to hold.
To go beyond the normal limits of something; to rise above and surpass what is ordinarily possible.
(of an illness or problem) lasting a long time or recurring constantly; not easily cured or resolved.
(of a condition) present from the time of birth, whether inherited or caused during development before birth.
To destroy or kill a large part of a group, population, or thing; to reduce drastically in number or strength.
To remove all moisture from something; to dry out completely, leaving it withered and lifeless.
To swell or stretch outward, especially because of pressure from inside; to cause a body part to bulge abnormally.
The state of being powerless to act, change, or prevent something.
Completely unable to act effectively or bring about change; lacking all power or influence.
(of a tumour or disease) tending to invade surrounding tissue and spread to other parts of the body; life-threatening.
To pretend to be ill or more seriously ill than one is in order to avoid work or duty.
At the point of death; in a state of dying.
To make the symptoms of a disease less severe without curing it; more broadly, to reduce the apparent seriousness of something without addressing the underlying cause.
The branch of medicine concerned with the causes and effects of diseases, especially as seen through laboratory analysis of body tissue.
A total or whole formed by combining many separate parts into one amount or group.
Not going as planned; wrong or off course.
To get around a rule, obstacle, or difficulty by finding a clever or indirect route rather than confronting it head-on.
